description: We are exchange students coming from University of Sussex, United Kingdom and currently studying in Waseda University as 3rd year students and our main subject area is Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence.
summary:
Astronauts experience significant muscle and bone loss due to prolonged exposure to microgravity, making physical deterioration one of the major health challenges of space exploration. While exercise is the most effective countermeasure, maintaining an efficient and personalized training routine in space remains challenging.

To address this, we developed SpaceMedical, an AI-powered astronaut health and fitness companion designed to support astronauts throughout their entire exercise journey.

The platform integrates health, sleep, body composition, and exercise performance data to provide personalized training recommendations through an AI coach. By monitoring environmental conditions, it can also identify favorable workout conditions, encourage astronauts to exercise at suitable times, and keep them motivated. During workouts, camera-based motion tracking helps astronauts verify their movements, monitor their technique, and track their progress, so they never feel lost.

Beyond daily training, SpaceMedical analyzes long-term patterns to identify the conditions under which each astronaut performs best, detect potential performance declines, and evaluate training effectiveness.

Our goal is to transform astronaut exercise from a fixed routine into an intelligent, adaptive, and data-driven system, helping preserve physical health, support mission performance, and enable safer, longer-duration space exploration.
details:
SpaceMedical is a health monitoring and exercise support platform designed to address one of the major challenges of long-duration space missions: muscle atrophy and bone density loss caused by prolonged exposure to microgravity.

Our platform monitors changes in muscle strength across different body regions while also tracking sleep, fatigue, cardiovascular measurements, nutrition, and recovery. Using these observations, it helps astronauts understand changes in their physical condition and provides evidence-informed exercise recommendations adapted to their needs.

An interactive body map allows astronauts to examine individual muscle groups and compare measurements over time. Our AI-assisted exercise planner considers these findings when suggesting training adjustments, while the MediaPipe-powered Posture Coach uses camera-based motion tracking to count repetitions and provide real-time exercise feedback.

SpaceMedical also incorporates historical NASA environmental data to provide additional mission context and motivational guidance. Workout results and feedback are stored, allowing astronauts to review their progress and support future training decisions.

We developed the application using React, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, SQLite, Google MediaPipe, and Docker, alongside NASA research resources and AI-assisted recommendation capabilities.

What makes SpaceMedical different is its integration of regional physical analysis, adaptive exercise guidance, environmental context, and real-time movement feedback into one platform.

Our prototype uses a clearly labeled 30-day simulated mission to demonstrate how these features work together. We prioritized scientific transparency, data privacy, practical usability, and the limitations of available measurements.

Our long-term goal is to help astronauts better preserve muscle strength and bone health through continuous monitoring, informed training adjustments, and personalized recovery support, contributing to safer and more sustainable human space exploration.
